Plain English

The words the game uses, without the wiki.

🧱Tier
Everything in IdleWorlds comes in 34 tiers — ores, cloth, gems, gear, zones. Tier 1 is copper-tier starter stuff; tier 34 is endgame. Higher tier = more XP per action, higher level to use.
⏱️Action
One completed loop of whatever you are doing: one ore mined, one bar smelted, one kill. Every rate in this toolkit is built up from a single action.
➕XP per task
A flat bonus your equipment adds to every action. Find it in-game under Character Stats. Flat bonuses are added first, then percentage bonuses multiply the total.
✖️Flat vs percent
Flat adds a fixed number (+24 XP). Percent multiplies what you already have (+25%). Flat matters most at low tiers; percent takes over later.
📈Effective XP/hr
XP per hour including the time spent gathering your own crafting inputs. It is the honest number — a recipe that needs 6 ores you have to mine yourself is slower than its raw rate suggests.
🌿Extra gather chance
A percentage chance to pull an extra resource from a gathering action. Over 100% it becomes guaranteed extras: 256% means 2 extra every time and a 56% shot at a third.
💎Socket
A slot in a piece of gear that holds a cut gem. Metal gear has one; tailoring armour has two, which is often what makes cloth win for stat-hunting builds.
⚔️Set bonus
Wear enough pieces of one tier and you get an extra stat on top. Smithing sets need 6 pieces, tailoring sets need 4. Mixing tiers breaks it.

Work-order production

Work Order Calculator

With thanks to Jvc2001 for providing the base model for this tab.

Compare how many complete work orders you could supply in 24 hours at one tier, including gathering, processing, crafting, Housing speed, and your live character bonuses.

ℹ️
Production benchmark, not a rotation forecast. IdleWorlds rotates available work-order professions. This view answers “how productive is each order type if I spend the full 24 hours supplying it?” and only counts complete order batches.

Where the 24 hours go. Processing means smelting bars or weaving cloth; crafting means brewing or making the final equipment piece.
Gold is calculated per completed work-order batch. Gold Find is then applied to the work-order reward.
Rules, assumptions & items.json data
Raw-material order100 ore / herb / fibre
Potion order20 potions
Equipment order1 requested gear item
Session86,400 seconds (24 hours)
  • 2x Gather Chance uses expected long-run yield: 1 + chance/100 resources per gathering action; values above 100% include guaranteed extra resources.
  • Bonus Brew is a chance for one extra potion and is capped at 100%, so expected output ranges from 1 to 2 potions per brewing action.
  • Housing uses the toolkit's shared live-game action-speed formula for 10-second gathering/processing/brewing actions and 180-second equipment crafts.
  • Early-tier Smithing/Tailoring recipes use their real T1–T4 material curves instead of assuming mature T5+ costs.
  • Turn-in gold is read directly from IdleWorlds items.json via work_order_turn_in_gold. That game-provided value already includes the profession turn-in bonus; the calculator only applies the submitted batch quantity and your Gold Find.
  • Fractional production is retained only as an expectation while calculating time. Work orders themselves are always floored to whole completed batches.
